sections.title: OH VALLEY TO MID ATLANTIC COAST
sections.text: EWD PROGRESSION OF WELL-DEFINED VORTICITY MAXIMUM OVER LAKE ONTARIO AND LARGER-SCALE SHORT WAVE TROUGH OVER ONTARIO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A CORRIDOR OF HEIGHT FALLS FROM THE LOWER GREAT LAKES INTO NEW ENGLAND DURING THE D1 PERIOD. IN THE LOW LEVELS...SURFACE LOW NEAR TORONTO WILL DEVELOP ENEWD...REACHING THE ADIRONDACKS BY EVENING WHILE TRAILING COLD FRONT ADVANCES SEWD THROUGH THE LOWER GREAT LAKES. LATE MORNING VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY AND RADAR DATA INDICATE GRADUALLY DEEPENING CONVECTION OVER PORTIONS OF WRN NY ALONG THE SRN FRINGE OF ABOVE-MENTIONED VORTICITY MAXIMUM WHERE TEMPERATURES HAVE WARMED TO AROUND 80 F. EXPECT A FURTHER INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY TODAY ALONG THE SRN FRINGE OF DENSER...MORE PERSISTENT CLOUDS /I.E. SRN NY INTO PA/ WHERE LOCALLY STRONG DIABATIC WARMING AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 70S WILL BOOST MLCAPE TO 1500-2500 J/KG. MOREOVER...THIS CORRIDOR WILL RESIDE ALONG SRN FRINGE OF 40-50 KT WLY MIDLEVEL WIND MAXIMUM ATTENDANT TO THE LAKE ONTARIO VORTICITY MAXIMUM...RESULTING IN SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR FOR ORGANIZED STORM MODES...INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND BOWING STRUCTURES. WHILE DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY HAZARD...A TORNADO OR T

sections.title: WRN DAKOTAS INTO THE NEB PNHDL
sections.text: NEUTRAL TO SLIGHT HEIGHT RISES ARE FORECAST ACROSS THE REGION TODAY IN WAKE OF SHORT WAVE TROUGH EXITING THE UPPER GREAT LAKES. HOWEVER...CONVERGENCE ALONG LEE TROUGH...STRONG DAYTIME HEATING AND OROGRAPHIC FORCING WILL EFFECTIVELY WEAKEN CAP WITH AT LEAST ISOLATED TSTM DEVELOPMENT ANTICIPATED BY LATE AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. THE PRESENCE OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ATOP A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WILL YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT INVOF LEE TROUGH LATER TODAY WITH MLCAPE OF 2000-2500 J/KG. WHEN COMBINED WITH A VERTICALLY VEERING WIND PROFILE AND 30-40 KT OF DEEP...WLY SHEAR...SETUP WILL FAVOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS.

sections.title: MIDDLE TX COAST
sections.text: PER LATEST NHC GUIDANCE...EXPECT TS DON TO CONTINUE WNWWD TO JUST NE OF LRD BY 30/12. AN ASSOCIATED INCREASE IN LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL GRADUALLY OVERSPREAD THE AREA LATER TODAY INTO TONIGHT N-E OF CENTER OF TS CIRCULATION. GIVEN THE VERY MOIST/LOW LCL THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT ALREADY IN PLACE...THE POTENTIAL FOR A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO WILL EXIST WITH ANY SUPERCELLS EMBEDDED WITHIN LAND FALLING RAIN BANDS. ..MEAD/GARNER.. 07/29/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS NWRN OK AND ERN KS
sections.text: ...NWRN OK AND ERN KS... ADDED A SMALL SLIGHT RISK TO ERN KS FOR A SLGTLY HIGHER PROBABILITY OF WIND DAMAGE THAN SURROUNDING AREAS. SURFACE OBSERVATIONS INDICATE WEAK SURFACE LOW WAS LOCATED NEAR SLN. TRAILING FRONT/BOUNDARY EXTENDED SWWD FROM THE LOW INTO NWRN OK...WITH WARM FRONT STRETCHING EWD INTO WRN MO SOUTH OF MCI. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO EXPAND IN COVERAGE ACROSS NWRN OK/ERN KS DUE TO LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND STRONG HEATING. TEMPERATURES NEAR 100 WERE RESULTING A DEEPLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER...WHICH WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR DAMAGING WINDS. ALTHOUGH DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS ONLY 15 TO 20 KT...CONVERGENCE MAY ALSO RESULT IN STORMS TO FORM INTO A LOOSELY ORGANIZED LINE OF STORMS. STORMS ARE THERMODYNAMICALLY DRIVEN...SO THEY SHOULD WEAKEN QUICKLY THIS EVENING. REFERENCE MD 1784 FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.

sections.title: PORTIONS OF IL/IN
sections.text: ALTHOUGH SOME STORM MODELS HAVE SHOWN STRONG CONVECTION DEVELOPING NEAR SURFACE FRONT OVER IL...MID/HIGH CLOUDS AND WEAKER CONVERGENCE HAVE RESTRICTED HEATING AND INHIBITED SURFACE BASED CUMULUS FROM DEVELOPING. ANY STORMS THAT DEVELOP CERTAINLY HAVE A POTENTIAL TO BE SEVERE...BUT CURRENT TRENDS SUGGEST THE MORE VIGOROUS CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE FROM OH EWD...SO LOWERED THE SEVERE PROBABILITIES FOR PORTIONS OF THIS REGION. REST OF OUTLOOK ON TRACK WITH ONLY MINOR CHANGES TO OUTLOOK LINES BASED ON LATEST CONVECTIVE TRENDS. ..IMY.. 07/29/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1154 AM CDT FRI JUL 29 2011/ CORRECTED FOR CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK GRAPHIC IN TX
